The fundamental semistable reduction theorem for Abelian varieties by Grothendieck shows that if A is an Abelian variety over the fraction field K of a discrete valuation ring \mathcal{O}, then there is a finite field extension L/K such that A_{(L)} = A \otimes_K L has semistable reduction over the integral closure \mathcal{O}_L of \mathcal{O} in L.Semistability here means more precisely that if \mathcal{A}_L is the Néron model of A_{(L)} over \mathcal{O}_L, then the fibres \mathcal{A}_{L,s} of \mathcal{A}_L over the closed points s\in S=\mathrm{Spec}(\mathcal{O}_L) (which are always a smooth algebraic group s) are extensions of Abelian varieties by tori. ...
